\subsubsection{Not Yet Verified}\label{sss:eis-open}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item \textbf{The runnable bench is not the whole channel.} Its feedback
    element is an ideal resistor set to the measured ladder value, which the
    campaign shows is worth \SI{0.019}{\percent} in the loop, and it carries no
    feedback capacitor. It is therefore faithful below the feedback pole and
    optimistic above a few kilohertz at the high-gain codes: at gain code 63 it
    reports \SI{2.73}{\percent} where the complete channel measures
    \SI{2.84}{\percent} at \SI{1}{\kilo\hertz}, and \SI{3.17}{\percent} against
    \SI{5.18}{\percent} at \SI{5}{\kilo\hertz}.
  \item \textbf{Current read as a code, demodulated.} The extracted converter
    does convert a live impedance record --- three conversions decoded while the
    transimpedance output moves \SI{317}{\milli\volt} peak to peak --- so the
    readout is alive, but no demodulated result exists at code level. Two
    obstacles, one structural: the converter multiplexer has no
    reference-electrode input (Section~\ref{sss:pixtop-adc}), so the potential
    channel can only be the commanded potential; and a coherent record of four
    excitation cycles at \num{64} conversions per cycle costs about
    \num{7.5} hours of simulation per multiplexer slot.
  \item \textbf{The reference-modulation term is unmodelled, not absent.} The
    supply regulator whose output moved \SI{25.8}{\milli\volt} with the code word
    (Section~\ref{sss:dacr2r12-supply}) has been deleted from the channel, and
    in this deck the ladder takes its reference from an ideal
    \SI{2.5}{\volt} rail; what the excitation table measures is the ladder's own
    linearity between two codes and nothing else. On silicon the term returns in
    proportion to the impedance between the regulator and the ladder, which is a
    fourth reason the calibration impedance is not optional.
  \item \textbf{Corners and mismatch.} Every number in this section is the
    nominal process point at \SI{37}{\celsius}. The mode adds no devices and the
    blocks it uses carry their own corner and Monte Carlo runs, but the
    measurement itself has been run at one point only, so nothing here bounds how
    the impedance error spreads across a wafer.
\end{itemize}
